q: What does an UPDATE do inside Postgres?
options: Writes a new version of the row and marks the old version as ended
Changes the row in place
Deletes the row and removes the space
Writes the change only to the log
why: The old version stays until it is cleaned. That is how readers can still see the old row.

q: In `xmin`, `xmax` and `ctid`, what does `xmin` tell you?
options: The smallest value in the column
Which transaction created this version of the row
Which transaction ended this version
Where the row lives on disk
why: xmin made it, xmax ended it, ctid is where it lives.

q: A table gets many updates and its file keeps growing. What is the cause?
options: Postgres compresses badly
Indexes are copied into the table
Dead rows pile up and nobody has cleaned them yet
Each connection keeps its own copy
why: Every UPDATE and DELETE leaves a dead row. Dead rows take space until someone cleans them.

q: What is the difference between VACUUM and VACUUM FULL?
options: VACUUM FULL is faster and safer
VACUUM deletes the table's indexes
They are the same, FULL just prints more text
VACUUM makes space reusable and keeps the file size. VACUUM FULL shrinks the file but rewrites the table and blocks it
why: Before you use VACUUM FULL, find out why autovacuum could not clean.

q: A transaction has been open for two days. How does it hurt the table?
options: It keeps every dead row that appeared since it started, so cleanup cannot remove them
It locks the whole table for writes
It makes all indexes invalid
It deletes old rows by accident
why: Find it with backend_xmin, and end it.
